justification: Changes what a served UI shows. Directionality: it ADDS the condition text the API already sent and reveals rows a React key collision was hiding, so it can only make a number more attributable, never less. No value is altered and nothing is written.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: DQ-32 is declared fixed, so the ledger goes RED if the jest guard fails: if the card stops rendering conditions, collapses rows sharing control_type + section_ref, or truncates without saying so. Mutation-tested END TO END, not just at the test: reverting DcpSnapshotCard.tsx and running dq_check.py produced RED naming DQ-32, and restoring it produced PASSED. Four of the five jest assertions fail against the old component; the fifth guards the inverse case (no spurious notice) and passes either way, recorded as weak.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The fixture is verbatim condition text from four real rows (sutherland_shire / residential_flat_building / car_parking, ids 246-249), not invented strings. DQ-32c's count comes from the live database.

pre_impl.existing_data: Traced every served path before changing anything. fetch_dcp_setbacks already returns every row with notes; /api/capacity/calculate `setbacks` already attaches `condition`; DcpStructuredControls.tsx (the main UI) already renders a condition column; /api/dcp/structured-controls:243 already sends `condition: row.notes || null`. On the live DB, 556 of 562 rows in ambiguous groups carry a condition and 6 do not.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The ledger's framing - 'the capacity engine returns a different zone's number' - was wrong, and re-deriving it has cost two sessions. Nothing picks one row. The defect was one card DROPPING a field, plus a React key collision hiding rows outright. A second assumption also failed: fixing /api/capacity/calculate looked like the user-facing half, but LepCapacityData is rendered nowhere, so that change is invisible to users and is recorded as shape-consistency rather than claimed as a fix.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new component, route or script. One interface field, one render block, one key, one cap made explicit; `cwd` is ~3 lines inside dq_check.py, which already runs in CI. DQ-32c reuses the existing probe registry.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The card already fails soft when the controls fetch errors; this change does not touch that path. DQ-32c exits 2 if the database is unreachable.

functions.name: DcpSnapshotCard
functions.what: Renders a council's numeric DCP controls under a duplex verdict, each with the condition stating which case it covers.
functions.input: lgaName, and an optional councilSlug used to fetch /api/dcp/structured-controls
functions.output: a card listing up to six controls, each with label, condition and value, plus a count of any not shown
functions.if_none: An uncovered council renders the request-capture form instead; a control with no condition renders the value alone, unchanged.
functions.edge_cases: control_type + section_ref is NOT unique - per-bedroom parking rates share both - so the key includes the index. Conditions are optional and absent ones render nothing.
functions.failure_mode: Read-only display. Its failure mode is showing less than it should, never a wrong number.

functions.name: run_one
functions.what: Runs one ledger check as a subprocess and maps its exit code to OK / RED / UNKNOWN.
functions.input: a DQ id and its spec, which may now carry an optional cwd relative to the repo root
functions.output: a verdict string and a detail string for the report
functions.if_none: No cwd means the repo root, exactly as before - existing checks are unaffected.
functions.edge_cases: jest resolves babel from the working directory, so --rootDir parses and then fails on every file; npm --prefix cannot be resolved by subprocess without a shell on Windows and reported UNRUNNABLE.
functions.failure_mode: A wrong cwd makes a check unrunnable, which is reported distinctly from passing.

break_it.scenario: A council holds four parking rates for one development type, separated only by bedroom count.
break_it.what_happens: Before: four identical 'Car parking' rows showing 1, 1.5, 2 and 0.25 with no way to tell which applied - and the React key collision meant only one was actually drawn.
break_it.how: The condition renders under each label, and the key includes the index.

break_it.scenario: A council has nineteen controls and the card caps at six.
break_it.what_happens: Six of nineteen looks exactly like all nineteen, so a reader has no reason to look for the row that applies to them.
break_it.how: It now states 'Showing 6 of 19 controls for this council.' The cap remains; the silence does not.
break_it.repro: the third assertion in the guard test

break_it.scenario: A row carries no condition at all.
break_it.what_happens: It sits beside a different value for the same control and cannot be attributed by any UI, however correct.
break_it.how: Not fixed - it needs a source lookup per row. Measured and tracked as DQ-32c: 6 rows (ids 10, 257, 259, 799, 2, 6) against 556 in the same groups that do state their case.

break_it.scenario: Someone reads the old DQ-32 count and plans weeks of PDF adjudication.
break_it.what_happens: 562 rows treated as 562 defects, when 556 are correct rows that simply state their case.
break_it.how: The ledger row now leads with the correction and DQ-32's check is the jest guard, not the row count.

break_it.scenario: The card regresses and stops passing the condition through again.
break_it.what_happens: Silent - nothing errors, the numbers still render, they just become unattributable again.
break_it.how: DQ-32 is declared fixed with the jest guard as its check, so dq_check.py goes RED in CI. Verified by reverting the component.

break_it.scenario: The capacity route's new condition fields are assumed to reach a user.
break_it.what_happens: Overclaiming a fix on a surface nobody sees.
break_it.how: LepCapacityData is rendered in no .tsx; recorded in the commit, the ledger and here as shape-consistency rather than a user-visible fix.

verified: 5 new jest assertions pass; 4 of 5 fail against the old component.
Whole ledger mutation-tested end to end: revert the card -> dq_check.py RED naming DQ-32; restore -> PASSED.
Full jest suite: 85 suites, 1117 tests, all passing.
Type check 8 errors against a baseline of 677; the 6 pre-existing capacity/route.ts errors are unchanged (confirmed by stashing).
DQ-32c returns 6 on the live database, against 556 rows in the same groups that carry a condition.
gaps: 6 rows still state no condition; they need a source lookup per row and are tracked as DQ-32c, not fixed here.
The fifth jest assertion passes against the old component too - it guards the inverse case only. Recorded as weak rather than counted as coverage.
The capacity route's parking/landscaping conditions reach no UI, so that half is untested by any rendering guard.
The conveyancing PDF was not audited for this defect class; only the web surfaces were traced.

post_merge.db_reset: No migration, no schema change, no write. Every database read in this change is a count.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open a duplex verdict for a Sutherland Shire address and confirm the parking rows each show their case beneath the label ('1 bedroom', 'visitor parking') rather than repeating 'Car parking' with bare numbers, and that a council with more than six controls says how many are not shown.
